clue.text: Obscure World War I soldiers move back

parts.note: the BEF was the British Expeditionary Force sent to France in 1914

indicators.note: back tells us the word for move is read in reverse

parts.note: to move is to go

explanation.surface: Someone reports that First World War troops retreated, and the details are kept vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal of the word for move; 'Obscure' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog something is to cloud it or make it unclear, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Settlement of parasite on some horse

parts.note: a bot is the larva of the botfly, a parasite of horses and sheep
some means any, as in 'have you any?'
a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A colony grows up of some parasite living on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Botany Bay, near Sydney, was the site named for the first British penal settlement in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany Bay was the place chosen for an Australian convict colony, a historical example of a settlement.

clue.text: Decisive and rich…

annotationWithheld.why: Decisive and rich… (5): FAT for rich leaves AL unclued; the A and L come from 'a novice' at the start of 3-down, words this clue as held does not contain

clue.text: … a novice environmentalist has only romantic notions initially

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmental party

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: An inexperienced campaigner for the planet has nothing but idealistic dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' at the start belongs with the ellipsis from 2-down and is no part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a raw beginner, a synonym for someone new to a job.

clue.text: A club -or it could be a spade

explanation.surface: A card game term pairs a weapon with a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackjack is a cosh or bludgeon; and the jack of spades is a black-suited jack, one card that qualifies.

clue.text: In speech, proposed law can appear essential

indicators.note: in speech says the words for proposed law and can are to be said out loud

parts.note: a bill is a proposed law and a tin is a can, together sounding like the hyphenated adjective

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill is put forward and can be presented as vital.
explanation.walkthrough: BILL TIN said aloud gives the answer; 'appear' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built-in is inherent or integral, an idiomatic match for essential.

clue.text: Approaches a meeting place on Sunday

parts.note: a venue is where people meet

explanation.surface: Someone describes how to get to a gathering spot on the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are ways of approach, both literally as tree-lined roads and figuratively as lines of attack.

clue.text: Without a second thought, pack a gift

indicators.note: without asks for the named letters to be taken out of the bag word

parts.note: a knapsack is a pack carried on the back
taken as written
PS is a postscript, a thought added after the letter is finished

explanation.surface: On impulse someone wraps up a present.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and PS from the middle of KNAPSACK leaves KN + ACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A knack is a natural talent or flair, a synonym for a gift.

clue.text: After a game, soldiers find referee at end to express regret

indicators.note: after puts the soldiers following the opening pair

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: at end picks the final letter of referee

explanation.surface: After a match, troops look to the official to say sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' only links; 'at end' supplies the E of referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to say sorry, which is how one voices contrition.

clue.text: Said to want work

indicators.note: said says the synonym for want is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to want is to need

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to be desperate for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead dough is to work it with the hands, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Like an exact copy of it, he let out

indicators.note: out implies the letters of the phrase before it are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone said a perfect replica was released by him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OFITHELET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait done to the life is a faithful likeness, an idiom for accuracy.

clue.text: A rambler perhaps moved upwards

parts.note: a rambler is a climbing rose, so a rose is one example

explanation.surface: A hiker climbs a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambler' looks like a walker, but it is a type of climbing rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning got up or ascended.

clue.text: Stuff available in any London store

indicators.note: store says the words any London keep the material within them

explanation.surface: A fabric can be bought in any shop in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'aNY LONdon'; 'available in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: One of 22 was carried, we hear, in an artery

parts.note: the answer to 22-down is cases, and a trunk is one kind of travelling case

indicators.note: we hear says the word for was carried is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: rode means travelled as a passenger

explanation.surface: A piece of luggage was transported along a main route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artery' looks medical, but it means a major road.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk road is a main highway, and an artery is a figurative term for a major route.

clue.text: Scholars meeting shortly? It's in the wind

parts.note: BAs are holders of Bachelor of Arts degrees
shortly means soon

explanation.surface: Academics are to meet soon, it is rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wind' suggests rumour, but it means the wind section of an orchestra; 'meeting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoon is a woodwind instrument, so it belongs in an orchestra's wind section.

clue.text: Upper-class involved in fishin' for marine creature

indicators.note: involved in places the class letter within the word for looking

parts.note: fishing for something is searching for it, with the final G dropped as in the clue

explanation.surface: A posh angler is out after sea life.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside SEARCHIN' to make SEA-URCHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny echinoderm living on the seabed.

clue.text: Tree doctor has received nothing since retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
has received puts zero inside the abbreviation for a doctor

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner
nil means nothing
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon has earned nothing since stopping work.
explanation.walkthrough: GNILPAS, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree.

clue.text: Star journalist caused people to adopt opposing views

definitions.text: caused people to adopt opposing views

parts.note: Polaris is the Pole Star
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A famous reporter split public opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise opinion is to divide it into two extreme camps.

clue.text: Be unused to being put in untidy stowage

indicators.note: being put in sets the short word inside the rearranged storage letters
untidy says the letters of stowage are in disorder

explanation.surface: Things go unused when stuffed in a messy store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' signals the anagram of stowage, and 'being put in' slots the short word into it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes to waste is not used and is lost, an idiom.

clue.text: Time chap wanted desperately

parts.note: a year is a period of time
Ned is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A clock-watching man longed for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned is to have longed or craved, a synonym for wanting badly.

clue.text: Attractive picture

explanation.surface: An appealing image.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing can mean pulling in, as a drawing card attracts crowds; and a drawing is a sketch.

clue.text: A prayer paid for by the recipient

explanation.surface: A plea is made down a reversed-charge telephone line.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short liturgical prayer; and calling collect means the person phoned pays.

clue.text: Smoke in bed with lady love

indicators.note: in places the woman and the zero inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
her refers to a woman
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone lights up in bed with their girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links the woman to the tennis zero, both of which go 'in' the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, something one smokes.

clue.text: Rail car — reckon it needs adaptation

indicators.note: needs adaptation says the letters of the phrase must be reworked

explanation.surface: A railway carriage is judged in need of modification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like railways, but a rail is a type of wading bird; 'it' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a bird of the rail family.

clue.text: Fold linen

explanation.surface: A folded sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a business collapse, as when a firm folds; and crash is a coarse linen fabric.

clue.text: Instances about three points

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about
S, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: Examples surround three key arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Cases are examples or occurrences, a synonym.

clue.text: Replace French man with Welsh

parts.note: René is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is swapped for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to put a fresh one in place of the old.

clue.text: Bottom right — one man can be seen climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters run upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone at the bottom of a hill is right to be seen going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be seen' links; RIDAN read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, so it means the bottom.

clue.text: The remains of a trophy

explanation.surface: What is left of a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left after burning; and the Ashes is the cricket trophy contested by England and Australia.

clue.text: Edmund's cavalry

explanation.surface: Soldiers on horseback belonging to a man called Edmund.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Ironside was an English king of 1016; Cromwell's Ironsides were his Civil War cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund II was nicknamed Ironside, so Edmund's is Ironside's; and Cromwell's horse troops were called the Ironsides.

clue.text: Hid things in different places, showing wisdom after the event

indicators.note: in different places says the letters of the two words are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone hid belongings around the house, then realised later where they should have been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding that comes only once something has happened.

clue.text: Song needs, say, clear backing

indicators.note: backing says the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: say means for example, written EG
to clear is to rid

explanation.surface: A melody calls for clear accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' links; EGRID read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song of lament, sung at a funeral.
